page: Microsoft Azure E20ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz, the instance supplies 20 dedicated vCPUs across 10 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory is configured at 160.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 extensions such as VNNI and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration through AES and SHA-NI. The instance includes 1182 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and operates without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core CPU throughput and memory performance. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1962.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3080.48, both positioning in the top performance quartile. PassMark memory testing measured 2775.61, corroborated by uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 76.66 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 55.94 GB/sec. Multi-core compute performance fell within the median range, generating 30802.17 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 12766.0 in multi-core Geekbench evaluations. Text generation on small 135M parameter language models recorded an above-average 331.24 tokens/sec, whereas prompt processing on large 70B models exhibited lower throughput at 5.46 tokens/sec.

The instance offers favorable resource density for memory-bound tasks due to its 8:1 memory-to-core allocation and onboard NVMe drive. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of discrete GPU acceleration and moderate multi-threaded compute limits, which restrict heavy deep learning model execution. Given its high RAM allocation and direct-attached storage, the server fits memory-intensive applications including relational database servers, Redis caching clusters, data engineering transformations, and high-throughput web backends.
